title: Audit event bridge: provenance & SIEM export heuristics (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft that collects heuristics and lightweight design notes for the "Audit Event Bridge" — a middleware layer that normalizes internal audit events (RBAC v2, evidence links, action metadata) into a canonical payload suitable for downstream SIEMs and evidence automation tooling. Goal is to capture provenance, make minimal but sufficient exports, and define versioning markers so consumers can safely roll forward/roll back.

Scope and constraints:
- Inputs: internal audit emitter (service-level events), RBAC v2 context enrichment, evidence attachments (links to blob store), and operational metadata (route, customer, environment).
- Outputs: one or more sidecar export formats (Elastic/CEF/JSON-LD), and an optional lightweight event envelope for streaming to Kafka/Splunk/SEIM API.
- Non-goals: full forensic archival (this remains in evidence store), user-facing UI changes. This is about export and schema compatibility layers.

Core principles (quick):
1) Minimal surface area: only include fields downstream consumers need to meet detection/use cases. Avoid exporting verbose model inputs/outputs.
2) Explicit provenance: every exported event must carry a provenance header (emitter_id, emitter_version, capture_ts, canonical_event_id, schema_version).
3) Stable identifiers: canonical_event_id uses UUIDv4 prefixed by emitter namespace; allows dedupe and idempotency.
4) Version delta markers: include schema_delta and compatibility_hint for consumers to do graceful parsing.
5) Evidence references as pointers: never inline large artifacts. Provide signed short-lived URLs + metadata (hash, size, mime).

Proposed canonical export schema (high level fields) — draft v0.1:
- schema_version: string (semver-like, e.g. "1.0.0")
- canonical_event_id: string (ns-uuid)
- emitter: string (service-name)
- emitter_version: string (git short hash or release tag)
- captured_at: ISO8601 timestamp (UTC)
- event_type: string (normalized taxonomy label)
- event_severity: string (low/medium/high/critical)
- rbac_context: object pointer (see rbac pointer pattern below)
- action: string (api_call / authz_decision / config_change / evidence_linked)
- actor: string (redwood user id / service principal)
- target: string (resource id)
- outcome: string (success/failure/partial)
- outcome_reason: short string (if failure)
- evidence_refs: array of pointers (signed_url, hash, size, summary)
- routing_metadata: array of tags (customer, region, tier)
- schema_delta: string (optional freeform)
- compatibility_hint: string (backcompat|breaking|adapter-required)

Note: agents.md requires flat JSON for storage metadata only; above internal high-level schema includes nested patterns that will be flattened in the bridge payload per downstream adapter (see Adapter section).

RBAC v2 enrichment pattern (heuristic):
- Minimal RBAC pointer: role_ids (list), policy_version, decision_path_hash. Dont export full policy text.
- If the decision involves resource-level allow/deny with attributes, add a condensed attribute map (<=8 keys).
- Add a link to a deterministic evaluation artifact (policy_evidence_ref) so auditors can replay the decision.

Evidence pointer pattern (example):
- evidence_refs[] = [{"name":"input_manifest","signed_url":"https://...","sha256":"hex","ttl":"5m","size_bytes":"432"}]
- For large model artifacts (tokens, model outputs) only include a 128-char summary and pointer.

SIEM export adapters (routing):
- Elastic JSON: full canonical payload but strip evidence_refs.signed_url (replace with evidence_id) and add evidence_meta reference to separate archival export.
- CEF mapping: map canonical_event_id -> deviceExternalId, event_type -> name, outcome -> outcome, include limited actor/target info; do not include user PII fields.
- Splunk HEC: tokenized envelope with schema_version and minimal routing tags; evidence pointers are separate HEC call to /evidence endpoint.

Versioning and rollforward strategy (how upgrades happen):
- Schema version is semver at major.minor.patch. Major increments = breaking change.
- Keep a compatibility_hint for 90-day deprecation window on minor changes that could affect consumers.
- Introduce schema_delta by adding additive fields only where possible. For breaking changes, produce a compatibility shim that emits both old and new fields for a period (default 90 days).
- Maintain a consumer registry (Confluence table) listing who depends on which schema_version. Automate compatibility checks via CI using unit examples.

Backward/forward compatibility heuristics:
- Consumers must ignore unknown fields.
- For renamed fields, include the old name as a deprecated alias for the deprecation window.
- Provide a small validation contract (json-schema) per version and publish a compact sample payload for tests.

Operational concerns and performance:
- Bridge should batch small events (sub-second grouping) to reduce SIEM API pressure, but keep latency SLO for critical authz events (<=200ms end-to-end export).
- Signed URLs must be generated lazily and cached for 30s before rotation to avoid frequent KMS calls.
- Throttle evidence-heavy flows with a token-bucket and fallback to queuing with TTL.

Security & Privacy guardrails:
- Explicit PII suppression: the bridge will run a configurable redaction set. Default: no raw prompts, no user email, no model full outputs.
- Access control: only services with "audit-exporter" role can consume evidence_signed_urls. RBAC v2 mapping required.
- Audit of exports: produce an export_audit record in the internal store linking canonical_event_id to export destinations and result status.

Open questions /议题 (todo):
- Q1: Which downstream consumers require full action inputs for detections vs. which can operate on summaries? (Need responses from SOC/DFIR)
- Q2: What is the retention policy for signed URLs created for evidence pointers? Current thought: 5–30 minutes depending on destination.
- Q3: How to handle cross-tenant events where customer tokens are present? (Masking strategy)
- Q4: Should schema_version be machine-readable (numeric) or string-based with tags?

Action items (owners & short timeline):
- Aisha: draft json-schema for v1.0 and sample payloads (due 2025-10-16).
- Evan: prototype Elastic + Splunk adapters and pressure-test using replay tool (due 2025-10-30).
- Diego: draft RBAC pointer contract and policy_evidence_ref format (due 2025-10-14).
- Maya: confirm SOC/DFIR detection requirements and list critical fields (due 2025-10-09).

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC-AUDIT-123 (audit event taxonomy master)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-987 (task: implement audit-export-adapter)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/543 (experimental bridge prototype)

Notes to self / fragments:
- consider using JSON-LD @context for long-term semantic mapping to make SIEM mapping easier.
- possible to include a small "fingerprint" computed over event-relevant fields to help dedupe across exporters.
- try to avoid emitting model prompt completions by default; only on explicit opt-in per customer with strong retention controls.

End of draft. This doc intentionally mixes heuristics and TODOs — it should be treated as an aggregator for the prototype phase.
